meta.title: CNN Magic Wall: From TED to Broadcast
meta.description: How a relationship formed after Jeff Han's breakthrough TED2006 demo brought Perceptive Pixel's platform to CNN—and gave Turner R&D and CNN Weather a new canvas for live forecasting.

hero.label: CNN · Technology Scouting & Product Development
hero.title: From a TED Demo to CNN's Magic Wall
hero.subtitle: After seeing Jeff Han unveil his breakthrough multi-touch interface at TED2006, I connected with him and brokered Perceptive Pixel's engagement with CNN. Turner R&D then designed and built the weather application with CNN Weather.

context.challenge: Move CNN beyond limited touchscreen experiments toward an interaction model that could support live broadcast storytelling.
context.scope: Technology scouting, relationship brokering, product direction, and interaction design leadership
context.team: Turner R&D and CNN Weather for the weather application; Perceptive Pixel and CNN for the election-night application
context.body: The relationship I built with Jeff Han after TED2006 became Perceptive Pixel's path into CNN. Turner R&D, under my direction, designed and built the weather application's UI in close collaboration with CNN Weather, whose meteorologists brought the domain expertise, on-air workflow, and presentation requirements. The person demonstrating the application in the video is CNN chief meteorologist Chad Myers. The election-night application that later made the wall famous was a separate collaboration between Perceptive Pixel and CNN.

sections.label: The Origin
sections.title: The technology was impossible to ignore.
sections.description: Jeff Han's TED2006 presentation was multi-touch's breakthrough public moment. The relationship formed after the talk became the introduction and engagement that brought Perceptive Pixel's platform into CNN.
sections.caption: Jeff Han, “The radical promise of the multi-touch interface,” TED2006.

sections.label: The Product
sections.title: Weather turned the wall into a broadcast tool.
sections.description: Turner R&D designed the interface and built the application in collaboration with CNN Weather. Together, the teams translated meteorologists' domain knowledge and on-air workflow into a direct, spatial way to move through forecasts, storm systems, maps, warnings, and supporting data while staying connected to the audience.
sections.caption: CNN chief meteorologist Chad Myers demonstrates the interactive weather application, designed and built by Turner R&D with CNN Weather.

sections.label: Inside the Product
sections.title: Designed for live manipulation.
sections.description: Development captures show the weather interface's map navigation, severe-weather warnings, drawing tools, and on-air controls—the working product behind the broadcast demonstration.

sections.label: Platform Adoption
sections.title: Election night made the wall famous.
sections.description: These 2007–2008 development and studio photographs document the election-night application created collaboratively by Perceptive Pixel and CNN. They show the platform's wider adoption at CNN; they do not depict the weather application designed by Turner R&D with CNN Weather.

sections.label: The Leadership Move
sections.title: The intervention began before interface design.
sections.description: The decisive work was recognizing that the technology choices under consideration would constrain the experience, finding a platform capable of the interaction model, and creating the relationship that allowed CNN to adopt it. Product leadership here meant shaping the conditions in which good interaction design could exist.
